title: Clutch-Time Performance Features for NBA Win Probability

sources.paper: Trends and Performance Visualization of Clutch Time in Japan's Professional B.League
sources.key_finding: Clutch time = last 5min with score margin <=5pts. Paint touches and 3PT efficiency remain efficient under pressure; mid-range drops. Useful for predicting game outcomes in close games.

sources.paper: Machine learning for sports betting: should model selection be based on accuracy or calibration?
sources.key_finding: Calibration-based model selection → +34.69% ROI vs -35.17% for accuracy-based. Validates Brier score as primary metric. Models trained on NBA multi-season data.

motivation: Current feature engine has no clutch-time breakdown. Close games (final 5min, margin<=5) are won by teams with superior clutch performance. This is predictive of future game outcomes and not captured in season-level or game-level box score averages.
data_source: NBA play-by-play (already in pipeline via Cat19 play-by-play)
implementation_notes: Filter pbp events to last 5 minutes where abs(home_score - away_score) <= 5
Compute eFG% = (FGM + 0.5*3PM) / FGA in clutch window, rolling 10 games
clutch_win_pct: wins in games that entered clutch window, last 10 such games
Normalize as delta (home - away) for directional features
rationale: High-leverage close games drive betting edge. Teams that win clutch time win more games than their season stats suggest. Feature is low-redundancy with existing categories.
cross_project_applicability: MEDIUM — political analog is 'final week polling surge' (last 7 days before election, margin <5pts). Similar clutch-time win pattern.
implementation_effort: MEDIUM — requires pbp aggregation by time window, 1-2 days implementation
status: PROPOSED — awaiting implementation on next Kaggle/Colab GPU run
